Idrakpur Fort
A Mughal-era river-fortification associated with the defence of the
Dhaka region. It is traditionally linked with Mir Jumla’s
seventeenth-century military works. Its compact brick structure and
bastion-like form make it a notable example of military architecture.
The fort stands within the urban area and is one of the district’s
best-known heritage sites. Check local opening arrangements before
visiting.
Courtgaon area, Munshiganj

Baba Adam Mosque
This historic mosque is associated with the memory of Baba Adam, a
Muslim preacher linked to the region’s medieval history. The building
is noted for its traditional brick construction and domed form. It is an
important example of the Islamic architectural heritage of Bikrampur.
The surrounding settlement gives visitors a sense of the area’s long
religious history. Please be respectful of worshippers and local
customs.
Kazi Kasba, Rampal Union,

Sonarang Twin
Temples
The twin temples are among the best-known Hindu heritage
structures in Munshiganj. Their tall forms and terracotta-era brickwork
make them distinctive in the surrounding rural landscape. They are
generally associated with the region’s historic Hindu patronage and
temple-building traditions. The site is especially interesting to visitors
who enjoy architecture and local history. The temples are in a village
setting, so access may involve narrow local roads.
Sonarang village, Tongibari
Upazila, Munshiganj, Munshiganj,
Bangladesh

Bikrampur Buddhist
Bihar and Museum of
Antiquities
Archaeological excavations at Raghurampur revealed remains
associated with an early Buddhist settlement in historic Bikrampur.
The nearby museum interprets finds and the area’s archaeological
significance. It offers a useful introduction to the region’s role in the
Buddhist and early medieval past of Bengal. The site is best visited
as a combined archaeology-and-history stop. Confirm museum
opening times before travelling.
Raghurampur, Rampal Union,

Shyamsiddhi Math
Shyamsiddhi Math is a prominent historic religious tower in the
district. Its tall, tapering profile is a landmark within the village
landscape. The structure reflects the region’s older Hindu religious
and architectural traditions. It is a worthwhile stop for visitors
exploring Munshiganj’s temples and zamindari-era heritage. As with
many village monuments, facilities and interpretation on site may be
limited.

Mawa Ferry Ghat and
Padma Riverfront
Mawa is a well-known riverfront destination on the Padma, popular
for wide river views and the lively ferry-terminal atmosphere. Visitors
come to watch boats, enjoy the breeze and sample local fish dishes.
The river landscape changes with season, current and shifting
sandbanks. It is a public transport and working river area, not a
managed beach. Keep away from unsafe edges and follow
ferry-terminal rules.
Mawa, Louhajang Upazila,
Munshiganj, Munshiganj,
Bangladesh

Padma Bridge
Viewpoint, Mawa side
The Mawa side offers views of the Padma Bridge corridor and the
broad river landscape. It is a convenient stop for photography and
observing one of Bangladesh’s major infrastructure projects. The best
viewpoints depend on access restrictions and current traffic
arrangements. Do not stop on the bridge carriageway or restricted
road shoulders. Use designated public areas and follow signs.
Mawa approach area, Louhajang
Upazila, Munshiganj, Munshiganj,
Bangladesh

Meghna Riverbank,
Gazaria
The Meghna riverbank in Gazaria provides expansive views of a
major river and its changing channels. The area is valued for boat
traffic, river scenery and a glimpse of river-based livelihoods. Visitors
may find local food stalls and informal stopping points near landing
areas. Facilities vary by location and season. Ask locally about safe
access because currents and banks can be hazardous.
Gazaria riverfront, Gazaria
Upazila, Munshiganj, Munshiganj,
Bangladesh

Rampal Dighi
Rampal Dighi is a large historic pond associated with the old
Bikrampur landscape. The waterbody and its banks offer a quiet
break from the busy town area. It also reflects the traditional
importance of large ponds for settlement, water and community life.
The surrounding area can be explored alongside nearby heritage
sites. It is a local public-space visit rather than a developed resort.
Rampal, Munshiganj Sadar,

Bangladesh

Bhagyakul Zamindar
Bari area
Bhagyakul is known for old zamindari residences and the cultural
history of prosperous riverine families. Remaining buildings and local
landmarks provide glimpses of the area’s past commercial
importance. The settlement is also a way to experience rural
Munshiganj beyond the main town. Some structures may be privately
occupied or altered, so access is not guaranteed. Ask permission
before entering any residential compound.
Bhagyakul, Sreenagar Upazila,

Bhawal Rajbari
Bhawal Rajbari is associated with the historic Bhawal Estate and its
influential zamindar family. The palace complex reflects the region’s
colonial-period administrative and landed heritage. Its location in
Joydebpur makes it one of Gazipur’s most recognisable historical
landmarks. The surviving buildings and grounds have changed over
time, so not every area may be accessible. Treat occupied or official
areas respectfully.
Joydebpur, Gazipur Sadar,
Gazipur, Gazipur, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Baliadi Zamindar Bari
Baliadi Zamindar Bari is a historic landed-estate residence associated
with the zamindari period. Its architecture and remaining compound
features recall the social and economic influence of local landlords.
The site is of interest to visitors tracing rural Bengal’s estate history.
Conditions and access can vary because parts may be privately
used. Confirm local access before making a special trip.
Baliadi, Kaliakair Upazila, Gazipur,
Gazipur, Bangladesh
Open map ■
St. Nicholas Church
St. Nicholas Church is a historic Christian place of worship in Nagari,
a settlement with a long Catholic community history. The church and
surrounding village offer insight into the region’s religious and cultural
diversity. Its significance is as much communal as architectural.
Visitors should dress modestly and avoid disrupting services. Check
with local caretakers before photography inside.
Nagari, Kaliganj Upazila, Gazipur,
Gazipur, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Bhawal Estate
heritage sites
The historic Bhawal estate shaped much of the social history of the
area around Joydebpur. Surviving estate-era buildings and
associated landmarks provide context for the famous Bhawal family
and its legacy. This is best understood as a dispersed heritage area
rather than one single monument. Some locations are now in active
institutional or private use. Use local guidance to identify accessible
structures.
Joydebpur and surrounding
Bhawal estate area, Gazipur,
Gazipur, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Nagari historic
Catholic settlement
Nagari is one of the older Christian settlements in the Dhaka region.
Its churches, community institutions and long-standing local traditions
form a distinctive cultural landscape. The settlement helps tell a
broader story of religious communities in Bengal. Visitors can
combine a respectful walk with nearby rural scenery. Access to
schools, church interiors and community property requires
permission.
Nagari, Kaliganj Upazila, Gazipur,
Gazipur, Bangladesh

Bangabandhu Sheikh
Mujib Safari Park
This large safari park is a major family attraction with animal exhibits
and landscaped visitor areas. It was designed to offer wildlife viewing
in a managed setting rather than a traditional zoo-only experience.
Visitors should follow park rules, stay within designated areas and
never feed animals. Opening arrangements and ticketing can change,
so check before travel. Allow several hours for a visit.
Mauna, Sreepur Upazila, Gazipur,
Gazipur, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Bhawal National Park
Bhawal National Park protects a large tract of sal forest north of
Dhaka. It is popular for day trips, nature walks, picnics and observing
the forest landscape. The park is especially attractive during cooler
months, although weekends can be crowded. Keep the forest clean
and avoid loud activity or damaging plants. Check current entry rules
and facilities with the forest authority.
Near Rajendrapur, Gazipur Sadar
and Sreepur area, Gazipur,

Nuhash Polli
Nuhash Polli is a retreat created by celebrated Bangladeshi writer
and filmmaker Humayun Ahmed. Its gardens, ponds, sculptures and
wooded setting give it a distinctive artistic atmosphere. Fans visit to
remember the writer and enjoy the landscaped grounds. Public
access may be limited or subject to specific opening arrangements.
Verify visiting permission before travelling.
Pirojoli, near Hotapara, Gazipur
Sadar, Gazipur, Gazipur,
Bangladesh

Bangladesh
Agricultural Research
Institute gardens and
grounds
The agricultural research campus is associated with Gazipur’s green
institutional landscape and agricultural research heritage. Visitors
should not assume the working campus is freely open as a tourist
site. With permission, the area may be of interest to those curious
about crop research and local horticulture. Access restrictions apply
because it is an operational institution. Contact the institution in
advance if planning an educational visit.
Joydebpur, Gazipur Sadar,
Gazipur, Gazipur, Bangladesh

Rajendrapur forest
picnic area
The Rajendrapur area is known for forest scenery and day-trip picnic
destinations near the Dhaka–Mymensingh corridor. Sal trees and
green spaces provide a break from the city. Some picnic facilities are
privately operated and may require booking. Visitor experience
depends on season, crowds and site management. Confirm the exact
venue and current entry arrangements before setting out.
Rajendrapur, Gazipur, Gazipur,
Bangladesh

Wari-Bateshwar
Archaeological Site
Wari-Bateshwar is one of Bangladesh’s most important early
archaeological landscapes. Excavations have uncovered ancient
settlement remains and artefacts suggesting long-distance trade
connections. The site is central to discussions of early urbanisation in
Bengal. Visitors should distinguish excavated areas from ordinary
village land and follow local guidance. Interpretation facilities may be
modest, so a guide can improve the visit.
Wari and Bateshwar villages,
Belabo Upazila, Narsingdi,
Narsingdi, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Parulia Mosque
Parulia Mosque is a historic religious structure recognised among the
district’s heritage places. Its traditional masonry and mosque form
reflect older local building practices. The mosque remains connected
to the surrounding community, so it should be treated first as a place
of worship. Architectural details are best appreciated with respectful,
unobtrusive observation. Ask before taking photographs inside.
Parulia, Shibpur Upazila,
Narsingdi, Narsingdi, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Lakshman Saha
Zamindar Bari
This historic zamindari residence is associated with the district’s
landed and merchant history. Surviving buildings and local accounts
provide a glimpse into the social life of the town in an earlier period.
The property may have been altered or repurposed over time. Access
can depend on current ownership and use. Confirm the precise
entrance locally before visiting.
Narsingdi town area, Narsingdi
Sadar, Narsingdi, Narsingdi,
Bangladesh

Baliakandi / historic
zamindari residences
of Shibpur
Shibpur and nearby villages contain historic residences associated
with local landholding families. These are generally dispersed
buildings rather than one formal heritage complex. Their value lies in
documenting local architecture and the rural social order of the past.
Some structures are privately occupied or in poor condition. Seek
local directions and permission before entering compounds.
Shibpur Upazila, Narsingdi,
Narsingdi, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Historic settlements
of Egarasindhur trade
corridor
The wider archaeological landscape around Wari-Bateshwar includes
settlement areas that help explain historic trade and habitation. The
district’s position near waterways supported movement of goods and
people. This entry refers to the broader heritage landscape, not a
single ticketed monument. Archaeological remains may be fragile or
not visibly marked. Visit with a knowledgeable local guide where
possible.
Belabo–Wari-Bateshwar area,
Narsingdi, Narsingdi, Bangladesh

Dream Holiday Park
Dream Holiday Park is a commercial amusement and family
recreation destination. It offers rides and leisure facilities suited to a
day trip. The experience is recreational rather than historical, making
it a clear contrast with the district’s archaeological sites. Rides and
amenities may vary by operating schedule. Check ticket prices,
opening days and ride availability before travelling.
Chaitaba, Madhabdi area,
Narsingdi, Narsingdi, Bangladesh

Meghna Riverfront,
Raipura
The Meghna riverfront offers views of boats, river traffic and broad
stretches of water. The landscape is closely tied to fishing, transport
and riverside settlements. It can be a scenic stop for photography and
observing everyday river life. There may be no formal visitor facilities
at smaller landing points. Check local advice on safe banks and boat
access.
Raipura riverbank area, Narsingdi,
Narsingdi, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Hatirdia and rural
countryside
The rural countryside around Hatirdia offers a look at agricultural
villages, ponds and seasonal greenery. It is suited to slow travel and
photography rather than a single organised attraction. Visitors can
learn about local markets and village life by exploring respectfully.
Transport and amenities are basic away from town centres. Ask
before photographing people or private property.
Hatirdia area, Monohardi Upazila,
Narsingdi, Narsingdi, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Narsingdi Railway
Station and town
centre
The town centre gives visitors a practical introduction to the district’s
busy commercial life. The railway station area reflects the role of rail
transport in connecting Narsingdi with Dhaka and other regional
centres. Nearby markets are useful for local snacks and everyday
shopping. This is an urban stop, not a managed sightseeing
attraction. Take care around roads, platforms and traffic.
Narsingdi town, Narsingdi Sadar,
Narsingdi, Narsingdi, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Meghna-Ghorashal
riverside landscape
The riverside landscape near Ghorashal is shaped by the Meghna
system and nearby industrial development. Visitors may find open
river views and activity around local crossings and settlements. It
offers a different perspective from the district’s ancient archaeological
sites. Access varies because some riverfront areas adjoin industrial
or private property. Use public access points and obey safety signs.
Ghorashal, Palash Upazila,
Narsingdi, Narsingdi, Bangladesh

Baliati Palace
Baliati Palace is one of the most important zamindar-era architectural
complexes in Bangladesh. Its multiple buildings, courtyards and
ornamental details reflect the wealth of the Baliati estate. The
complex developed over generations and is a major heritage
destination for architecture enthusiasts. Some areas may be under
conservation or subject to visitor rules. Check opening arrangements
and respect protected structures.
Baliati, Saturia Upazila, Manikganj,
Manikganj, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Teota Zamindar Bari
Teota Zamindar Bari is a historic estate complex associated with the
Teota zamindar family. The surviving structures show the scale and
style of rural elite residences in Bengal. The village is also linked in
popular accounts with poet Jibanananda Das’s family history. Parts of
the complex may be occupied or deteriorated. Ask locally about safe,
permitted areas to visit.
Teota village, Shibalaya Upazila,
Manikganj, Manikganj, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Machain Mosque
Machain Mosque is a historic mosque known within Manikganj’s local
architectural heritage. Its traditional form and setting make it useful
for understanding the spread of Islamic religious architecture in rural
Bengal. It remains part of a living community, so visitors should be
discreet. Architectural features may be easier to appreciate with local
explanation. Confirm directions because village roads can be narrow.
Machain village, Harirampur
Upazila, Manikganj, Manikganj,
Bangladesh
Open map ■
Dhankora Zamindar
Bari
Dhankora Zamindar Bari is associated with the region’s landed-estate
history. Remaining buildings and local memories illustrate the social
prominence of zamindar families before the end of the zamindari
system. The site is less formalised than major heritage monuments.
Some parts may be private residences. Obtain permission before
entering buildings or courtyards.
Dhankora, Saturia Upazila,
Manikganj, Manikganj, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Historic Teota village
heritage area
Teota’s historic village landscape includes estate-era buildings and
local heritage connected with prominent families. The setting helps
place the zamindar residence within the surrounding community
rather than viewing it in isolation. Visitors may find old structures
mixed with modern homes. The area is not a single managed
museum. Explore on foot only where public access is clear.
Teota, Shibalaya Upazila,
Manikganj, Manikganj, Bangladesh

Aricha Ghat
Aricha Ghat is a major river transport area where visitors can watch
ferries, launches and working river traffic. The meeting of roads,
boats and river scenery gives the place a lively atmosphere. It is
especially interesting for photography and observing transport life.
This is an operational terminal, not a recreational beach. Stay within
public areas and follow ferry staff instructions.
Aricha, Shibalaya Upazila,
Manikganj, Manikganj, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Padma Riverbank,
Harirampur
The Padma riverbank offers wide views of water, sandbars and a
changing river landscape. Seasonal erosion and sediment movement
constantly reshape the chars. Visitors may enjoy boat views and rural
scenery, but access can change quickly. Boat trips should be
arranged with trusted local operators. Avoid unstable banks and heed
weather and current conditions.
Harirampur riverbank and char
areas, Manikganj, Manikganj,
Bangladesh

Kaliganga Riverfront
The Kaliganga riverfront is a convenient place to see the waterways
that shape the district. Riverside views vary with water level and
season. Nearby town facilities make it easier to combine the visit with
local food or markets. It is an informal public landscape rather than a
developed attraction. Choose safe access points and avoid slippery
embankments.
Manikganj town and nearby
riverbank, Manikganj Sadar,
Manikganj, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Baliati Palace
grounds and gardens
Beyond its historical significance, Baliati’s courtyards and open
grounds offer a scenic setting for photography and a relaxed visit.
The scale of the complex makes it easy to spend time exploring
exterior details. Its landscaped and architectural setting is a strong
contrast to riverfront attractions. Follow conservation instructions and
do not climb on old masonry. Visitor access can vary by maintenance
work.
Baliati, Saturia Upazila, Manikganj,
Manikganj, Bangladesh
Open map ■
Saturia rural
landscape
Saturia’s villages offer ponds, fields, orchards and a slower rural
atmosphere. The area is a useful complement to a visit to Baliati
Palace. Seasonal crops and monsoon water create different scenery
through the year. It is not a single designated tourist facility, so plan
around local roads and transport. Respect private land and local
residents.
Saturia Upazila, Manikganj,
Manikganj, Bangladesh

Rudrakar Math
Rudrakar is known for a historic math or monastic-style religious
structure and long-standing Hindu traditions. The site forms part of
the district’s documented cultural heritage. Its importance is local and
architectural as well as religious. Festivals may make the area
especially active at certain times. Visit respectfully and ask before
photographing worshippers.
Rudrakar, Shariatpur Sadar
Upazila, Shariatpur, Shariatpur,
Bangladesh

Kedar Roy's House /
moat remains
Local historical accounts connect this area with Kedar Roy, a notable
ruler of the Bhati region. Remains associated with an abandoned
residence and moat are described in district heritage records. The
landscape has been affected by river changes and later settlement. It
is not a fully conserved palace complex, and visible remains may be
limited. Seek local guidance to identify the site accurately.
Kedarpur area, Naria Upazila,
Shariatpur, Shariatpur,
Bangladesh

Dhanuka heritage
village
Dhanuka is recorded as a historic cultural settlement associated with
scholars and traditional learning. The village’s heritage is tied to
people, religious traditions and local institutions rather than one large
monument. Visitors interested in regional history can learn from local
residents. Specific buildings may be privately owned or altered. Ask
permission before entering homes or religious compounds.
Dhanuka, Shariatpur Sadar
Upazila, Shariatpur, Shariatpur,
Bangladesh

Mahisar historic
religious area
Mahisar is noted in district heritage accounts for historic ponds and
religious landmarks. Local tradition links the area with earlier regional
rulers and waterworks. The place reflects the importance of tanks and
sacred sites in older settlements. It is a dispersed village heritage
area, not a formal archaeological park. Verify the exact landmark with
local residents before travel.
Mahisar, Bhedarganj Upazila,
Shariatpur, Shariatpur,
Bangladesh
Open map ■
Koras / Kurashi
temple heritage area
Kurashi is mentioned in district heritage descriptions for old temples
and Shiva-linga-related religious remains. The site represents the
district’s Hindu cultural history and village worship traditions.
Surviving features may be small or incorporated into active religious
compounds. Visitors should be mindful of local customs. Directions
and public access are best confirmed locally.
Kurashi area, Shariatpur District,
Shariatpur, Bangladesh

Padma River char
landscape
The Padma creates a dramatic river landscape of broad channels
and shifting sandbars. Visitors come for river views, boat scenes and
rural photography. The chars and banks change with seasons and
erosion, so the scenery is never quite the same. Boat travel should be
arranged with local operators who understand the current. Avoid
unstable banks and follow safety advice.
Padma riverbank and char areas,
Naria and Zajira Upazilas,
Shariatpur, Shariatpur,

Meghna Riverbank
The Meghna riverfront offers open water views and a close look at
river-based livelihoods. Fishing boats, landing points and changing
light make it attractive for photography. It is an informal scenic area
rather than a managed park. Facilities and access vary by village and
season. Stay clear of active jetties and strong currents.
Bhedarganj riverfront area,
Shariatpur, Shariatpur,
Bangladesh
Open map ■
Kartickpur riverside
area
Kartickpur is a local riverside destination where visitors can
experience the district’s riverine setting. The appeal is the landscape,
boat activity and quieter village atmosphere. It can be combined with
a wider exploration of Bhedarganj. It does not have the facilities of a
formal resort. Ask locally about safe access and transport.
Kartickpur, Bhedarganj Upazila,
Shariatpur, Shariatpur,
Bangladesh
Open map ■
Naria river erosion
and riverfront
viewpoints
The Naria riverfront illustrates how the Padma’s erosion and shifting
channels affect settlements and land. It is an important landscape for
understanding the district’s relationship with the river. Visitors should
observe from safe, authorised areas rather than unstable
embankments. Conditions can change after heavy rain or high water.
Local guidance is essential.
Naria Upazila riverbank,
Shariatpur, Shariatpur,
Bangladesh

Shariatpur town parks
and public spaces
The district town provides small public spaces, local markets and a
base for exploring surrounding heritage villages. Visitors can
experience everyday local life and sample regional food. This is a
practical leisure stop rather than a single landmark. Facilities and
ambience vary by time of day. Combine it with nearby historical
locations for a fuller itinerary.
Shariatpur Sadar town, Shariatpur,
Shariatpur, Bangladesh

Rajarama Temple
Rajarama Temple is widely described as one of Madaripur’s oldest
